findings_to_judge.claim: Zepp set its H2 2026 margin expectations on 8 June 2026 with CFO Leon Deng naming memory as the specific gross-margin risk ("we expect higher memory costs to create near-term pressure on gross margins, driven by the industry-wide transition from DDR4 to DDR5 and high-bandwidth memory") and naming ASP increases plus a possible tariff refund as the offsets; since that date the consumer DRAM squeeze has escalated sharply — TrendForce on 22 June 2026 said consumer DRAM shortages had cascaded all the way down to DDR2 (contract prices +35-40% QoQ in 3Q26) and that OEMs/ODMs were substituting DDR4 designs with DDR3 and DDR3 with DDR2 to hold system cost. Zepp's gross margin had already fallen from a company-record 40.4% in Q4 2025 to 37.7% in Q1 2026, so the 1 September margin print and the H2 margin commentary are being made into a materially worse cost environment than the one management described in June.

The Balance 3 / Balance Ultra family, announced 2 June 2026 and presented as 'launched' in the Q1 release six days later, did not actually go on sale until the turn of June and July 2026 (Balance Ultra and Balance 3 Stainless Steel at the turn of the month, Balance 3 Titanium 'a few weeks later'). So the quarter being reported on 1 September carries essentially none of the new flagship line, while Q3 is the first quarter to carry both $599.99 SKUs (Balance Ultra and Cheetah 2 Ultra) — against a backdrop where portfolio ASPs rose more than 20% YoY in Q1 2026 and all seven 2026 launches were holding at MSRP with no discounting.

Zepp quietly exited Oura's ITC Section 337 case: Oura and Zepp jointly asked the ITC to terminate Zepp from Investigation No. 337-TA-1468 on 9 July 2026 and the administrative law judge granted it on 10 July 2026, removing the risk of a US limited exclusion order against the Amazfit Helio Ring ahead of the Helio Ring 2 and Helio Strap 2 launches confirmed for H2 2026. Terms were not disclosed, so a settlement or royalty charge could surface in the Q3 numbers rather than Q2.

The share repurchase authorisation that management still describes as active is effectively dormant: Zepp had used US$16.0m of the US$20m program as of 30 June 2025 and only US$17.0m as of 31 March 2026 — about US$1m of buying across nine months during which the ADS fell roughly 90% — leaving US$3m of capacity on a program that expires in November 2026. Shares outstanding are down only 1.66% year over year (14.66m ADS, market cap ~US$72m) against US$103.2m of cash at 31 March 2026.

Point72 Asset Management, Point72 Capital Advisors and Steven A. Cohen filed Amendment No. 2 to their Schedule 13G on 14 August 2026 reporting 0.00 shares and 0% of ZEPP as of 30 June 2026 — a full exit. The remaining 13G-scale holder disclosed in the same August window is Morgan Stanley / Morgan Stanley Capital Services at 8.8% with shared voting and dispositive power, i.e. a dealer/swap position rather than a fundamental one.
